projects_root.label: Projects folder
projects_root.hint: Where new project folders usually go

chat.label: Chat / API, no tools (Claude, ChatGPT)
chat.preamble: You can't run commands or edit files here. For any step that needs a command, give me the exact command and wait for me to paste the output. When you change a file, give the whole file (or a unified diff for a large file) in a fenced block headed with its path.

local.label: Local model (Ollama / LM Studio)
local.preamble: You can't run commands or edit files. Give me exact commands and wait for the output. Give changed files in full, in fenced blocks headed with their path. Keep explanations short.

roles.lead: Owns the plan, the questions to me, the hand-offs and the final report. Doesn't write the main code when the team has a coder.
roles.coder: Writes the change and its tests, following the project's existing patterns. Keeps the diff focused on this request.
roles.reviewer: Reviews the diff cold: correctness, edge cases, error handling, security, readability, and the acceptance criteria. Reports findings as blocker / should fix / nit with file:line. Doesn't rewrite the code.
roles.qa: Owns the test plan and acceptance criteria. Runs the checks and reports pass / fail per criterion with evidence. Doesn't fix code; sends failures back to the coder.
roles.security: Looks for injection, secrets in code or logs, unsafe deserialization, path traversal, missing auth checks and vulnerable dependencies.
roles.docs: Keeps README, CHANGELOG and comments in step with the change.

C#.outdated: dotnet list package --outdated --include-transitive; dotnet list package --deprecated; dotnet list package --vulnerable
C#.notes: Nullable reference types on; follow .editorconfig; async all the way down for I/O.

C++.outdated: check the vcpkg.json / conanfile baseline against the latest registry versions
C++.notes: Modern C++ (RAII, smart pointers, no raw new/delete); match the repo's C++ standard and .clang-format.

Rust.outdated: cargo outdated (cargo install cargo-outdated) and cargo audit (cargo install cargo-audit)
Rust.notes: No unwrap()/expect() in library code paths without a reason; keep unsafe to a minimum and document it.

Python.notes: Type hints on public functions; use a virtual environment; pin versions in requirements / pyproject.

Java.outdated: gradlew dependencyUpdates (ben-manes plugin) or mvn versions:display-dependency-updates
Java.notes: Match the repo's Java version; prefer records and Optional over nulls in new code.

TypeScript.notes: strict mode; no any without a reason; keep the lockfile in sync via npm, not by hand.

JavaScript.notes: Keep the lockfile in sync via npm, not by hand.

Go.notes: Handle every error; wrap with %w; keep packages small.

repo_path.label: Repo folder
repo_path.hint: For a new project, the folder to create

rules_file.label: Agent rules file
rules_file.hint: CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md in the repo

project_rules.label: Project rules (one per line)
project_rules.hint: Added to the Rules of every prompt for this project

title.label: Title
title.hint: Short name; also used for the branch

rules.Small: Small change: keep the process in proportion. At most one round of questions, a short plan, tests for what changed, docs only where touched, short updates.
rules.Large: Large change: write the plan first and wait for my OK before writing code. Commit in reviewable steps.

acceptance.label: Acceptance criteria
acceptance.hint: Given / When / Then, one per line. QA tests against these.

files.label: Files / folders in scope
files.hint: One per line. Blank = the agent finds them

reference.label: Reference / example code
reference.hint: One per line: code to copy patterns from

removal_plan.label: Removal plan for the old feature
removal_plan.section: Removal plan for the old feature

rules.Deep (line by line, incl. tests): Deep review: go line by line, including the tests, and check each test really asserts the behavior it claims to.

rules.No, minor and patch only: Stay within the current major versions. List the major upgrades you skipped.

handoff_notes.label: What's already done / current state
handoff_notes.hint: Shown to the agent as hand-off context

global_rules: Work only inside {repo_path} and the paths named in this prompt.
If something you need is missing, ask me everything in ONE message before writing code, each question with your recommended answer.
Follow {rules_file} and the project's existing patterns. Don't over-engineer and don't refactor code this request doesn't need.
Don't say something works until you've tested it. Only report facts you've verified (test results, counts, links).
If a step fails, stop and tell me which step and the exact error.
Never print, hardcode or commit secrets; read them from environment variables and keep them out of git.
Never force-push, rewrite history on {base_branch}, or merge a PR unless I say so.
Preserve existing line endings and file encoding.

orient.title: Get oriented
orient.text: In {repo_path}, read {rules_file} and README.md if they exist, then the code this request touches. Summarize the current state in 3-5 lines.

questions.title: Ask questions
questions.text: If anything you need is missing or unclear, ask me everything in ONE message, each question with your recommended answer so I can just reply 'yes'. Wait for my answers before writing code.

sync_base.title: Update base branch
sync_base.text: Make sure the working tree is clean (if it isn't, stop and tell me). Then `git checkout {base_branch}` and `git pull` (skip the pull if there's no remote yet).
sync_base.manual: I'll bring {base_branch} up to date myself. Don't pull or switch branches.

create_branch.title: Create branch
create_branch.manual: I'll create `{branch}` myself and switch to it. Don't create or switch branches.

plan.title: Plan
plan.text: Write a short plan: files to change, approach, risks, and how each acceptance criterion will be checked. Assign the work to the team.

implement.title: Implement
implement.text: Make the change. Follow the project's existing patterns and {language} conventions, and keep the diff focused on this request.

tests.title: Tests
tests.text: Add or update automated tests for each acceptance criterion and the edge cases you can think of.{test_plan_note} Run `{test_cmd}` and report pass / fail counts.
tests.manual: I'll run the tests. Write them, then give me the command and what to look for.

build.title: Build + lint
build.text: Run `{build_cmd}` and `{lint_cmd}`. Fix errors and warnings your change introduced; list pre-existing ones without fixing them.
build.manual: I'll build. Give me the commands and wait for my results.

review.title: Code review
review.text: Review the full diff against {base_branch} as if seeing it for the first time: correctness, edge cases, error handling, security, naming, tests, and whether each acceptance criterion is met. List findings as blocker / should fix / nit with file:line. The coder fixes blockers and should-fixes, then review once more. After two rounds, stop and list what's left.

qa.title: QA
qa.text: Check every acceptance criterion and test scenario: pass / fail with evidence (test name, command output, or the steps you ran). Send failures back to the coder and re-test after the fix.

docs.title: Docs
docs.text: Update README, CHANGELOG and comments only where behavior or usage changed.

commit.title: Commit
commit.text: Commit in small, logical commits with Conventional Commit messages (`{commit_type}: <summary>`).{issue_note}
commit.manual: I'll commit. Give me the list of changed files and a commit message (`{commit_type}: <summary>`).

push.title: Push
push.manual: I'll push `{branch}` myself. Tell me when it's ready.

create_pr.title: Open PR
create_pr.text: Open a PR with `gh pr create --base {base_branch} --head {branch}`. Title: `{commit_type}: <summary>`. Body: ## Summary, ## Changes, ## Testing (commands and results), ## Acceptance criteria (a checklist, ticked only when verified).{closes_note} Give me the link.
create_pr.manual: Give me the compare link ({compare_link}), a PR title and a markdown body (## Summary, ## Changes, ## Testing, ## Acceptance criteria).{closes_note} I'll open it and send you the link. Wait for it.

ci_check.title: Check CI
ci_check.text: If the repo has GitHub Actions, wait for the PR checks (`gh pr checks --watch`). If one fails, read the log (`gh run view --log-failed`), fix it, push and check again.

post_review.title: Post review on GitHub
post_review.text: Post the review on PR {pr} as ONE review with event COMMENT (not APPROVE or REQUEST_CHANGES): inline comments for line-specific findings and a summary body with the verdict. Use `gh api repos/{github_repo}/pulls/<number>/reviews` with a JSON body of event, body and comments (path, line, side, body).{reviewer_note}
post_review.manual: Don't post anything. Give me the review as markdown (verdict first, then findings with file:line) for me to paste.

verdict.title: Approve / request changes
verdict.text: Submit the verdict as the reviewer account {github_reviewer}: `GH_TOKEN="$(gh auth token --user {github_reviewer})" gh pr review {pr} --approve`, or the same with `--request-changes --body "<summary>"`. Never print the token or run `gh auth token` on its own. If {github_reviewer} wrote the PR, GitHub won't allow this; just tell me the verdict.
verdict.manual: Give me your verdict (approve / request changes) in one line with the reason. I'll submit it.

write_agents.title: Save team as agent files
write_agents.text: Create `.claude/agents/<name>.md` in {repo_path} for each teammate ({team_names}): YAML front matter with name, description (the role and when to use it) and model if one is listed, then the role brief as the body. Commit them so the team can be reused in this repo.

templates.name: New software - create a project
templates.description: Requirements -> scaffold the folder and repo -> build it as a team -> tests, review, QA -> GitHub repo -> optional CI.
rules: Pick current, well-maintained dependencies, and only as many as the requirements need.
Work on {base_branch} until the GitHub repo exists; use branches after that.

steps.text: Before scaffolding, check the requirements and acceptance criteria are complete and testable. Ask me everything that's missing in ONE message, each with your recommended answer, and wait.

steps.title: Scaffold project
steps.text: Create {repo_path} (stop if it exists and isn't empty). Set up a {language} {app_type}{framework_note} with the standard layout for that toolchain, a .gitignore for {language}, README.md (what it is, how to build, run and test), LICENSE ({license}) and {rules_file} listing the build / test / lint commands and conventions. Run `git init -b {base_branch}` and make the first commit.

steps.title: Architecture
steps.text: Propose the structure: modules, key types, data flow, and dependencies with versions. Keep it as simple as the requirements allow. Map each acceptance criterion to where it's implemented and how it's tested.

steps.title: Create GitHub repo
steps.text: Create the GitHub repo and push: `gh repo create {github_repo} --{visibility} --source "{repo_path}" --push`.
steps.manual: I'll create the GitHub repo myself. Give me the settings to use, then wait.

steps.title: Set up CI
steps.text: Add `.github/workflows/ci.yml` that runs `{build_cmd}`, `{lint_cmd}` and `{test_cmd}` on pushes to {base_branch} and on PRs, on {ci_os}, with dependency caching and the current major versions of the official actions. Push it and confirm the first run passes (`gh run watch`).

templates.name: Feature - add new
templates.description: Branch -> plan -> implement + tests -> review -> QA against acceptance criteria -> PR.

templates.name: Feature - change existing
templates.description: Change how an existing feature behaves: find every usage first, then change, test, review, QA, PR.
rules: If a change would break saved data, settings or a public API, stop and tell me before making it.

steps.title: Find usages
steps.text: List every caller, setting, saved-data format and doc that depends on the current behavior. This is what the change can break.
Change the behavior from current to new. Update tests that encoded the old behavior and say which ones changed and why.

templates.name: Feature - replace old with new (keep old alive)
templates.description: Build the new feature next to the old one behind a switch, prove parity, deprecate the old one without removing it.
rules: The old feature must keep working exactly as before while the switch is on 'old'.
Don't delete the old code in this request.

steps.title: Map the old feature
steps.text: List everything that uses the old feature (callers, config, saved data, docs). That's the compatibility surface the new feature has to respect.

steps.title: Build new behind a switch
steps.text: Build the new feature alongside the old one, selected by the switch described in Context. The default stays on the OLD path unless I say otherwise. Only touch the old code to route it through the switch.

steps.title: Parity tests
steps.text: Write tests that run both paths with the same inputs and compare the results. List every intentional difference.
steps.manual: I'll run the parity tests. Write them and tell me how to run both paths.

steps.title: Deprecate old
steps.text: Mark the old feature deprecated the way {language} allows (attribute, annotation, doc comment or a one-time log warning) with a pointer to the new one. Don't remove it.
Document how to switch, how to roll back, and the removal plan (mine if it's given above, otherwise propose one).

templates.name: Bug - fix a known bug
templates.description: Reproduce with a failing test -> root cause -> smallest fix -> regression test -> review -> QA -> PR.
rules: Fix the root cause, not the symptom. Don't change unrelated behavior.

steps.title: Reproduce
steps.text: Reproduce the bug from the details above. Write a failing test that shows it BEFORE changing any code. If you can't reproduce it, stop and tell me what you tried.

steps.title: Root cause
steps.text: Find the root cause and explain it in 2-3 lines. Check whether the same mistake appears anywhere else and list those places.

steps.title: Fix
steps.text: Make the smallest fix for the root cause.
Confirm the failing test now passes, add tests for any other places with the same mistake, then run `{test_cmd}` and report pass / fail counts.

templates.name: Bug hunt - review code for bugs (multiple reviewers)
templates.description: Independent reviewers -> consolidate -> verify with repros -> ranked report. Fixing waits for your go.
rules: Don't change any code until I pick which findings to fix.

steps.text: In {repo_path}, read {rules_file} and README.md if they exist, then map the code in scope (files listed in Context, or the whole repo if none). Summarize what it does in 3-5 lines.

steps.title: Independent reviews
steps.text: Every reviewer reviews the scope on their own, without seeing the others' findings. Look for logic errors, off-by-one, null / None handling, error handling and resource leaks, concurrency, input validation, security, and the focus areas. For each finding: file:line, what's wrong, a concrete input that triggers it, severity and confidence.

steps.title: Consolidate
steps.text: Merge the findings, remove duplicates and rank by severity. A finding is 'confirmed' only if two reviewers found it or it's been reproduced; everything else is 'suspected'.

steps.title: Verify
steps.text: For every high or medium finding, write a failing test or exact repro steps. Downgrade anything you can't reproduce.
steps.manual: I'll verify. Give me the repro steps for each high / medium finding.

steps.title: Report
steps.text: Give me the ranked list (confirmed, then suspected) with a proposed fix and effort for each. Then stop and wait for me to pick which ones to fix.

steps.title: Fix the ones I pick
steps.text: After I choose: create `{branch}` from {base_branch}, fix the chosen findings with a regression test for each, run `{test_cmd}`, commit (`fix: <summary>`), push and open a PR listing each finding fixed.

templates.name: QA - test plan and acceptance
templates.description: Turn the acceptance criteria into a test plan, automate what can be automated, run it, and give a verdict. QA doesn't fix code.
rules: QA reports bugs; it doesn't fix product code. Test code is fine.

steps.text: In {repo_path}, read {rules_file} and README.md if they exist, check out what's under test (see Context) and read the change. Summarize what changed in 3-5 lines.

steps.title: Check the criteria
steps.text: Check every acceptance criterion is testable (Given / When / Then). Rewrite vague ones and show me the rewrites before testing.

steps.title: Write the test plan
steps.text: Write the test plan as a table: id | scenario | steps | expected | type (unit / integration / manual) | criterion covered. Cover the happy path, edge cases, error paths, and regressions in nearby features.

steps.title: Automate
steps.text: Automate every scenario that can be automated, then run `{test_cmd}`.
steps.manual: I'll run the automated tests. Write them and give me the command.

steps.title: Run the plan
steps.text: Run every scenario and record pass / fail with evidence.

steps.title: QA verdict
steps.text: Give the verdict: pass / pass with issues / fail. List failing criteria and every bug found (title, repro steps, severity).

steps.title: Save the plan in the repo
steps.text: Save the test plan and results as docs/test-plans/<date>-<title>.md and commit it.

steps.title: Post verdict on the PR
steps.text: Post the QA verdict and the test-plan table as a comment on PR {pr} (`gh pr comment {pr} --body-file <file>`).

templates.name: Dependencies - update / replace obsolete packages
templates.description: Baseline -> inventory outdated, deprecated and vulnerable packages -> update in groups -> migrate code -> regression test -> PR.
rules: Prefer actively maintained packages; don't add a dependency where the standard library does the job.
Update lockfiles with the package manager, never by hand.

steps.title: Baseline
steps.text: Before changing anything, run `{build_cmd}` and `{test_cmd}` and record the results as the baseline.
steps.manual: I'll run the baseline build and tests. Give me the commands.

steps.title: Inventory
steps.text: List outdated, deprecated and vulnerable packages ({outdated_cmd}) as a table: package | current | latest | reason (outdated / deprecated / CVE) | breaking?. For deprecated or abandoned packages, propose a maintained replacement with one line of reasoning.
Show me the inventory and the replacements you propose, and wait for my OK before updating.

steps.title: Update in groups
steps.text: Update one package (or one related group) at a time. For major versions, read the changelog / migration guide first and list the breaking changes that affect this code.

steps.title: Migrate code
steps.text: Update the code to the new APIs. Don't leave deprecated calls behind; list any you couldn't replace and why.
Run `{test_cmd}` and compare with the baseline: no new failures. Add tests where a migration changed behavior.

steps.title: Regression check
steps.text: Run the app's main flows (or the test plan) and compare with the baseline. Report anything that behaves differently.
Commit one package or group per commit (`chore(deps): bump <package> <old> -> <new>`).{issue_note}

Open a PR with `gh pr create --base {base_branch} --head {branch}`. Title: `chore(deps): <summary>`. Body: the package table, breaking changes handled, code changes, and test results against the baseline.{closes_note} Give me the link.

templates.name: PR review - my code or another agent's
templates.description: Read the PR, build and test it, review it (one or more reviewers), post comments; approving needs a second GitHub account.
rules: Don't push commits to the PR branch unless I ask; review only.

steps.title: Read the PR
steps.text: Run `gh pr view {pr}` and `gh pr diff {pr}`, and read the description and any linked issue. If you need to run it, `gh pr checkout {pr}` (note the branch you were on first).
steps.manual: I'll give you the diff. Wait for me to paste it.

steps.title: Build + test the PR
steps.text: On the PR branch, run `{build_cmd}`, `{lint_cmd}` and `{test_cmd}`. Report failures; don't fix them.

Each reviewer reviews the PR on their own: correctness, edge cases, error handling, security, tests, and the acceptance criteria / focus areas if given. Then the lead merges the findings into one list (blocker / should fix / nit, file:line, suggested fix) and drops duplicates.

Post the merged review on PR {pr} as ONE review with event COMMENT: inline comments for line-specific findings and a summary body with the verdict. Use `gh api repos/{github_repo}/pulls/<number>/reviews` with a JSON body of event, body and comments (path, line, side, body).{reviewer_note}

steps.title: Put things back
steps.text: Switch back to the branch you started on.

templates.name: Refactor / cleanup (no behavior change)
templates.description: Baseline tests -> small refactor steps with tests green after each -> review confirms no behavior change -> PR.
rules: Behavior must not change. If a test has to change, stop and tell me why.

steps.title: Baseline tests
steps.text: Run `{test_cmd}` and record the result. If the code in scope has no tests, add characterization tests first.
steps.manual: I'll run the baseline tests. Give me the command.

steps.title: Refactor
steps.text: Refactor in small steps, running the tests after each one. Keep public APIs unchanged unless the plan says otherwise.
Review the diff against {base_branch} and confirm behavior hasn't changed: same inputs give the same outputs, errors and side effects. List findings as blocker / should fix / nit with file:line.

templates.name: Spike / research (no product code)
templates.description: Answer a question: compare options, optionally prototype on a throwaway branch, recommend.

steps.title: Research
steps.text: Answer the question. Compare the options in a table (pros, cons, effort, risk, maintenance, license) and say which you'd pick and why.

steps.title: Prototype
steps.text: Build a throwaway prototype on `{branch}` to prove the riskiest assumption. Don't merge it.

steps.title: Write-up
steps.text: Give me: the recommendation, the evidence, open questions, and the next request I should create (title + acceptance criteria).

templates.name: Release - version, changelog, tag
templates.description: Work out the version -> changelog -> bump -> build + test -> PR -> after merge: tag and GitHub release.

steps.title: Work out the version
steps.text: Use the version given in Context if there is one; otherwise work it out from the commits since the last tag (`git describe --tags --abbrev=0`) and tell me.

steps.title: Changelog
steps.text: Update CHANGELOG.md from the commits since the last tag (Added / Changed / Fixed / Removed).

steps.title: Bump version
steps.text: Bump the version in the project files.

steps.title: Tag + GitHub release
steps.text: Wait until I tell you the PR is merged. Then tag `v<version>` on {base_branch}, push the tag, and run `gh release create v<version>` with the changelog section as the notes. Attach build artifacts if the project produces them.
steps.manual: I'll tag and publish the release. Give me the commands and the release notes.

templates.name: CI / build setup (GitHub Actions)
templates.description: Add a build + lint + test workflow, make it pass, and suggest branch protection.
rules: Pin the official actions to their current major version.

steps.title: Write the workflow
steps.text: Add `.github/workflows/ci.yml` that runs `{build_cmd}`, `{lint_cmd}` and `{test_cmd}` on pushes to {base_branch} and on PRs, on {ci_os}, with dependency caching.
steps.manual: I'll add the workflow. Give me the YAML.

steps.title: Branch protection
steps.text: Suggest branch protection for {base_branch} (require CI, require a PR) and give me the `gh api` command. Don't apply it.

templates.name: Pick up where I left off
templates.description: Short prompt for after you've done a manual step (opened a PR, tested, merged) and want the agent to continue.

steps.title: Check current state
steps.text: Before doing anything, check git branch / status and the latest commit in {repo_path}, and the PR if there is one. Tell me if anything doesn't match what I described.

steps.title: Do the next thing
steps.text: Do what's under 'What to do next'.

templates.name: Taskmaskitator - board change (server + page)
templates.description: Taskmaskitator only. Back up the databases -> plan -> change server.py and index.html together -> pytest (Azure stubbed) -> live check on a scratch copy (port 8802) -> review -> docs (CHANGELOG, README, AGENTS.md) -> commit, push and open the PR -> stop so I can restart, test and merge.
rules: Workspace writes go under _write_lock in one transaction with one bump_rev, so open browsers pick them up on their next /api/rev poll. Never start a timer, close an interval or park another machine's ticket as a side effect.
Azure DevOps is read-only unless this request says otherwise; don't touch the time-stamping flow (azureQueue / postAzureComment) unless asked. Tests stub _azure_request with an obviously fake PAT.
Type hints on new public Python functions. Every new <input> gets a distinct name="ttb-..." and autocomplete="off".

steps.text: In {repo_path}, read AGENTS.md, the top of CHANGELOG.md and the README sections this request touches, then the code it touches in code/server.py and code/index.html. Check `git status` and the branch. Read the progress log C:\Sandbox\_AgentProgress\taskmaskitator\<branch>_Progress.md if it exists and carry on from its next step. (<branch> = the branch name with any / replaced by -). Summarize the current state in 3-5 lines.

steps.title: Back up the databases
steps.text: Before running anything against data, back up databases/auth.db and databases/workspaces/*.db with the SQLite backup API from a read-only source (?mode=ro) to C:\Sandbox\_AgentProgress\taskmaskitator\backups\<branch>\ (<branch> = the branch name with any / replaced by -), run PRAGMA integrity_check on each copy, and report the result.
steps.manual: I'll back up databases/ myself. Tell me when you need it and wait.

steps.text: Make the change in code/server.py and code/index.html together, following the surrounding patterns. Where the server now builds something the page also builds (e.g. a ticket's shape), say so in a comment in both places. Keep the diff to this request.

Write a scenario table (input -> expected result) for each acceptance criterion and the edge cases.{test_plan_note} Add pytest tests in tests/ using the srv fixture in tests/conftest.py (real server, temp databases, Azure stubbed via _azure_request; nothing reaches the network or databases/). Run `{test_cmd}` and report pass / fail per scenario plus the total.
Run `{build_cmd}` (there is no linter). Fix errors your change introduced; list pre-existing ones without fixing them.

steps.title: Live check on a scratch copy
steps.text: Copy code/ and the backup from the previous step into a scratch folder outside the repo. In each scratch workspace DB set app_config 'report' enabled to false BEFORE starting it, so it can't email anyone. Run the copy with `{run_cmd}` from that folder. Sign in by minting a session or connect token directly in the scratch auth.db (never use my password), then exercise each acceptance criterion through the API and in the browser, and check the console and server log for errors and for any token or PAT. Anything that reads Azure must be read-only. Afterwards stop the server and delete the scratch folder and any token files: they hold real data and secrets.
steps.manual: I'll test it on my instance. Give me numbered steps, what success looks like, and what to paste back.

steps.text: Follow the Documentation rule in AGENTS.md: a CHANGELOG.md entry under the current branch's 'Unreleased' heading (date, server / client / both, what it does for me, new endpoints, in-place schema upgrades); update the README section the feature belongs to (new endpoints go in 'API for agents and scripts') and remove anything the change made untrue; update AGENTS.md if a command, rule or workflow changed.

steps.title: Progress log
steps.text: Append to the progress log C:\Sandbox\_AgentProgress\taskmaskitator\<branch>_Progress.md (create it if needed): date, backup path, what changed (files and functions), test counts, live-check results, anything found but not fixed, and the next step.

steps.title: Stop for my test
steps.text: Stop here. Tell me whether I need to restart the service (server.py changed) or only reload the page (index.html only), give me numbered test steps with what success looks like, and list anything found but not fixed with a recommendation. Give me the PR link; I merge it.
